tldr: A lab on building Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol agents in Java with LangChain4j and the A2A Java SDK across Spring Boot and Quarkus, plus a Python agent and a router.
summary: Participants build A2A-compliant agents, starting with the protocol's core: implementing an AgentCard for discovery and an AgentCardExecutor for message delivery. They then deploy the same capability contracts on Spring Boot, JA2A and Quarkus, and connect a Python agent built with the A2A Python SDK to show cross-language interaction.

The lab continues with a dynamic router agent that decomposes multi-turn tasks and dispatches them across the mesh, and finishes with Day-2 operations: distributed state management, load balancing for stateful LLM conversations and tracing with OpenTelemetry.
keyPoints: A2A defines the wire format for interoperable multi-agent systems.
Agents expose an AgentCard and an AgentCardExecutor using the A2A Java SDK and LangChain4j.
The same agent contracts run on Spring Boot, JA2A and Quarkus and interoperate with a Python agent.
A router agent decomposes and delegates tasks; OpenTelemetry traces the interactions.
takeaways: Expose one of your agents with an AgentCard so other frameworks can discover it.
watchIf: You want to build interoperable multi-agent systems in Java.
